resources.string: Lets the Verdroid agent tap, swipe, type and read what is on screen when you ask it to automate a task on this phone. Nothing is sent anywhere except to the AI model you configured, as part of the task.

A profile bundles tools, skills, a model, instructions and memory, so you can switch with one tap at the top of a chat. Each chat remembers its profile. With only Default, nothing changes.
Its chats move to Default and the memories it learned become visible to \"All memories\" profiles. Chats and memories are not deleted.
Tried first; if it fails, the rest of Model priority is used. A chat\'s own pinned model still wins.
A chat\'s Tool presets can still override this; Settings → Tools switches still apply.
Selected only: the agent sees just these long-term memories, and anything it learns in this profile is added here (hidden from other profiles). Short-term notes are always per chat.

Short-term memory: the agent\'s scratchpad for one chat (task progress, decisions, findings). Always in that chat\'s prompt (~1k tokens, oldest trimmed) and deleted with the chat.
No short-term notes for this chat.
Long-term memory: lasting facts about you and your preferences, shared by all chats. The ~20 most important/recent go into the system prompt; the agent can search the rest. Exported to %1$s.

Shizuku\'s rish lets Verdroid run privileged shell commands (rish_run). In Shizuku, open “Use Shizuku in terminal apps” → Export files into Download, Documents or Documents/Verdroid/Input and tap Find rish (needs All files access), or pick the exported rish file (select rish_shizuku.dex too if asked). Verdroid copies both to /data/local/tmp/verdroid_rish and chmod +x (needs Shizuku).

Runs a model on this phone: GGUF files with llama.cpp, .litertlm files with Google LiteRT-LM. Private and offline, but much slower and less capable than cloud models. Suggested: Qwen3-4B Q4_K_M (≈2.5 GB, needs ~6 GB RAM) or a 1–2B model on older phones. Agents get a smaller tool set on local models. If a local model can\'t load, Verdroid moves on to the next model in Model priority.
The file is copied into Verdroid\'s private storage. .litertlm models come from the LiteRT Community on Hugging Face (huggingface.co/litert-community).
Experimental. GGUF: Vulkan, tested first in a separate process. LiteRT: its GPU (OpenCL) backend. On any GPU problem Verdroid uses the CPU instead.
Removes the copied model file (%1$s) from Verdroid\'s storage and from Model priority.

While a task runs, a foreground service shows \"Working on: <chat>\" with the current step and a Stop button. When nothing is running there is no service and no notification.

Tried top to bottom. On 429 / 5xx / upstream errors the next model is used and the failed one cools down.
kilo:… models use the Kilo Gateway with no API key. Kilo requests this hour: %1$d/%2$d.
Keys are stored encrypted (Android Keystore + EncryptedSharedPreferences). The primary key is used first; others are used in order when a key is rate-limited.

kilo:kilo-auto/free is in Model priority and is used when OpenRouter has no key or is unavailable. It works without an OpenRouter key (about 200 requests/hour). Kilo\'s free models may log prompts and replies, which can include your memories. Turn off \"Send memories to Kilo models\" below or remove the model from Model priority if you prefer.

The agent can split broad research into tasks run in parallel by sub-agents (spawn_subagents). Sub-agents only get the read-only tools selected below, cannot start other sub-agents, and stop when the main task is cancelled.
Max concurrent: %1$d (extra tasks wait in a queue)

All OpenRouter free-model calls (main chat, sub-agents, research workers) share one paced queue, because OpenRouter limits free models per account (20 requests/min). On a 429 a worker waits for Retry-After and retries instead of failing. Free models default to %1$d parallel workers until you move a slider.
Auto reads the provider\'s rate-limit headers, speeds up slowly after successes and halves on a 429. Learned rates are remembered per model.
If a sub-agent or worker is still rate-limited after its retries, it finishes on the Model priority list.

deep_research plans sub-questions with the main model, runs parallel workers (web_search + web_fetch) on the worker model, dedupes and filters URLs, then writes a long cited report to Documents/Verdroid/Output/Research. The agent calls it when you ask for research or a report (say \"deep\" or \"thorough\" for deep mode). Stop cancels every worker.
Same as sub-agent model (tip: a free model, e.g. openrouter/free)
Standard: time budget %1$d min (then the report is written with what exists)
Parallel workers: %1$d (lower if you hit rate limits)
